data.title: Stock Futures Rise as Optimism Improves Ahead of Anthropic Trading Debut
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Nasdaq futures led a rally in U.S. stocks premarket, after Anthropic's pricing of its hotly anticipated listing lifted confidence around the artificial-intelligence trade.

Anthropic's expectation-beating IPO pricing helped investor focus shift away from the AI jitters that have weighed on stocks so far this week. However, sentiment was tempered by hawkish Federal Reserve meeting minutes Wednesday that added to fears of extended policy tightening.

Nasdaq futures jumped 1.9% as chip makers and cloud-computing stocks rallied premarket. Anthropic sold more shares at a higher price than anticipated, implying a value of $1.5 trillion for the company. S&P 500 futures were also in the green--up 1.1%--as the index looks to turn the tide on a fifth-straight day of losses. Contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.6%. The index has fallen by more than 1% for three days in a row.

Equities were mixed across Asia, where the tech-dominated Nikkei Stock Average in Japan and South Korea's Kospi both closed in the green. Stock indexes in Hong Kong and Shanghai fell, however. In Europe, major indexes were all in the green. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 rose 0.5%.

Treasury yields ticked higher after falling in Asian trade, as investors respond to a hawkish readout from the Fed's October meeting. Near-term rate-sensitive two-year yields rose above 4.800%, while 10-year yields nudged back toward 5.100%. Thirty-year yields hovered around 5.420%.

Oil prices ticked slightly higher, picking up from falls Wednesday after U.S. crude oil inventories rose for a second consecutive week. The benchmark Brent crude contract rose 0.5% to trade around $92.40 a barrel, while the West Texas Intermediate contract nudged up 0.4% to trade around $83.50 a barrel.

The dollar fell slightly, but remained close to its highest level against a basket of global currencies since January 2025. Copper prices steadied after falling sharply in the last session but gold extended losses, trading close to $3,700 a troy ounce. Bitcoin rallied after recent declines, adding 2% to trade around $63,750.

Anthropic's trading debut will be in focus for the day ahead. Investors will also watch for readouts from the trilateral meeting between President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.

Write to Joe Stonor at josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com

data.title: Lenovo CEO Says AI Demand Is Broadening, Not Slowing
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Many tech industry insiders are worried about a slowdown in demand for the infrastructure hardware that power artificial intelligence. Lenovo's chief executive isn't one of them.

Instead, he sees AI-related demand broadening.

AI computing is moving beyond a handful of cloud service providers, increasingly being used by businesses and starting to be integrated into personal devices, Lenovo CEO Yang Yuanqing said in an interview.

Yang remains upbeat about the outlook for AI-related hardware, even as the global tech supply chain faces challenges from export controls, tariffs and national security reviews.

As more companies move from experimenting with chatbots to deploying AI for business operations, graduating from coding tools to AI agents, enterprise is becoming an increasingly important driver for Lenovo.

The PC maker's infrastructure-solutions business, which includes data-center hardware like AI servers, has become its biggest revenue and profit driver in recent quarters. In the fiscal second quarter, segment revenue more than doubled from a year earlier.

A breakdown shows that revenue from enterprise customers surged 200%, outpacing the 170% growth from cloud-service providers.

For Yang, that could mark a turning point for enterprises to become another driver for its AI server business. This is particularly important for Lenovo, as using trained models to complete various tasks, known as inferencing, creates demand for AI servers even after the initial model-training phase is completed.

Addressing market concerns about how geopolitical disruptions to chip supplies could affect AI-related demand, Yang said he sees no near-term impact for Lenovo.

Fresh worries about supply-chain disruptions surfaced earlier this week after the U.S. stepped up efforts to close loopholes via which advanced chips could be sent to China unlawfully, sparking concern about a spillover across the AI ecosystem.

Yang said Lenovo is well insulated from any potential fallout as it sources components globally and manufactures products close by to where it sells them. The company has over 30 manufacturing sites.

Another prevailing worry is that a shift in power in the U.S. government after the midterm elections could lead to more regulations that will slow the data-center buildout, slowing AI investment.

On that front, Yang said he can't predict the direction of policymaking, but that as AI use spreads, demand for it will persist.

"AI democratization is definitely the trend," he said.

For Lenovo, the next trend Yang wants to capitalize on is the integration of AI computing in smartphones and laptops. As that gradually occurs, the CEO bets devices will be an increasingly important growth engine for Lenovo, and the wider industry.

"In the long run, devices will become part of the broad AI infrastructure," catalyzing a new growth cycle, he said.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: NSE sees record natural gas options volumes, captures over 52% market share
data.description:
Shares of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) were up nearly 5% at the day's high on Thursday, November 19, after the exchange reported a record performance in natural gas options trading on its November 18 expiry session.

NSE recorded its highest-ever natural gas options volume of 39.9 lakh contracts during the session, crossing the 50% market share mark for the first time.

The exchange also registered a peak intraday open interest of more than 1.25 lakh contracts, translating into margin engagement of over ₹1,285 crore.

Premium turnover crossed ₹880 crore, with NSE capturing a market share of 52.23%.

The latest figures represent a more than twofold increase in premium turnover compared with the previous monthly expiry on October 21, when NSE recorded ₹440.14 crore.

On October 21, NSE accounted for 22.79 lakh natural gas contracts, representing a 38.36% market share, while the Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) recorded 36.63 lakh contracts, or a 61.64% share.

NSE's open interest stood at 71,656 contracts during that expiry session, compared with 3.70 lakh contracts on MCX.

data.title: Romania's Neptun Deep gas to boost exports, could curb LNG flows north, S&P says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Romania's Neptun Deep gas to bolster export role — S&P Global Energy
  • Additional gas supply could limit need for US LNG
  • Brussels says Neptun Deep to help growth, cut external deficit
  • Black Sea security risks mount

By Luiza Ilie

Romania's Black Sea Neptun Deep gas project will strengthen the country's role as a regional exporter, including to Ukraine, from 2027 and could cut the need for LNG shipped north via Greece, S&P Global Energy said.

Neptun Deep, with an estimated 100 billion cubic meters of recoverable gas, will double Romania's gas production and rank among the European Union's most significant energy deposits.

The project is a joint venture between OMV Petrom , majority-controlled by Austria's OMV , and Romania's state-owned Romgaz .

While Romgaz will use its share of the gas to supply domestic gas-fired power plants and a fertiliser maker, OMV Petrom also has long-term contracts to supply Germany and Moldova, with other European countries showing interest.

"Additional Romanian supply could reduce the need for some LNG volumes to move north via Greece and the Vertical Corridor, where cumulative transportation costs are high," S&P Global Energy told Reuters.

The Vertical Gas Corridor is a European gas infrastructure project designed to move liquefied natural gas from the United States and other non-Russian sources north from Greece into Central and Eastern Europe and Ukraine.

Earlier this week, the European Commission said Neptun Deep production will support a rebound in Romania's economic growth next year and help lower its external deficit.

Neptun Deep, which challenges Russian gas in the region, is exposed to security risks as the escalating maritime war between Russia and Ukraine is expanding into a major challenge for NATO in the Black Sea. The war has left littoral NATO member states such as Romania and Bulgaria vulnerable.

In August, the Romanian military intervened twice to destroy air and naval drones near Neptun Deep.

"We see the Black Sea is under strong assault. I am referring to drone attacks, ships that have been hit, sailors who have lost their lives, we see pressure on critical infrastructure including Neptun Deep," Romanian President Nicusor Dan said on Thursday.

"There is a need for deterrence efforts."

data.title: Slow-motion Uniper exit may be Berlin's better bet
data.description:
By Yawen Chen

Germany must shrink its stake in the rescued utility but wants to retain influence over €6 bln of planned investment. An auction could fetch up to €14 bln. Selling shares in the market, perhaps with the help of cornerstone investors, is preferable if valuations are similar.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow Yawen Chen on Bluesky and LinkedIn.

CONTEXT NEWS

German state-owned energy group Uniper said on November 16 that it planned around €6 billion of capital expenditure through the early 2030s, with 60% to 70% earmarked for flexible power generation, mainly gas-fired plants.

Uniper also said it expected adjusted EBITDA of between €1.2 billion and €1.5 billion in 2027, and between €1.2 billion and €1.6 billion "in the medium term".

The company, which received a €13.5 billion ($15.1 billion) bailout from the German government in 2022, set a new dividend policy on November 6. It will target annual dividend growth of 7% and proposed to pay €0.77 a share for 2026, compared with €0.72 for 2025.

data.title: Forint steadies, strong dollar continues to hurt FX
data.description:
Central European currencies steadied at lower levels on Thursday, remaining under pressure from the firming US dollar, with the forint trading near a multi-week low after Hungary's central bank signalled a possible interest rate cut.

On Tuesday, the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) left its base rate unchanged at 5.5%, as expected, but flagged it could have more scope to ease monetary policy when it updates its inflation forecasts in December.

The forint was up 0.1% against the euro at 0845 GMT, remaining near a 1-1/2-month low of 369.30 hit in the previous session.

Analysts at brokerage Equilor put the next euro/forint resistance levels at 369.50 and then 371.

PRESSURE REMAINS ON FX, BONDS

The Polish zloty was steady at 4.4130 per euro, after touching a two-week low of 4.4150 in early trading.

Polish state development bank BGK said the depreciation trend remained the baseline scenario, reinforced by recent unfavorable news on Poland's credit rating and the country's weakening fiscal standing.

Elsewhere, the Czech crown edged 0.1% lower to 24.4150 per euro, moving back towards a five-week low set earlier this week, while the Romanian leu remained steady at 5.3480 per euro.

Currencies continued to be held in check by the euro/dollar, which remained below the psychological 1.10 level. Analysts at ING said market bets on higher US interest rates were sapping emerging market currencies.

In bond markets, Czech yields continued to climb, with the benchmark 10-year yield gradually rising to nearly 5.30% since reaching a two-month low of 5.07% on November 10. (CZ10YT=RR)

"Today, the core rates are little changed relative to the local close, so we’re neutral on the rates. However, we expect the pressure on (Czech government bonds) to continue," Komercni Banka trader Marek Lesko said in a note, adding plans for secondary market auctions on Thursday had also weighed on bonds.

data.title: Holding firm Exor to raise bioMerieux stake to around 8.5%
data.description:
Investment company Exor said on Thursday it was raising its stake in bioMérieux to 8.53% from 3.87%, with the aim of becoming a long-term investor, citing confidence in the French biotechnology firm.

The transaction will be carried out through an exchange of Exor's shares and voting rights in Institut Mérieux for those in bioMérieux. Institut Mérieux will remain bioMérieux's majority shareholder with 55.24% of the share capital and 68.67% of voting rights.

  • The deal is expected to be completed in December, with Exor set to increase its voting rights in bioMérieux to 5.35%

  • The investment arm of Italy's Agnelli family currently holds a 10% stake and 5.3% of voting rights in Institut Mérieux

  • After completion of the deal, it will hold 5.02% of Institut Merieux's shares and 2.58% of voting rights

  • Exor values bioMerieux greatly for its leadership in diagnostics and wants to support it over the long term, CEO John Elkann said

data.title: Johnson Matthey boosts guidance as interim earnings spike
data.description:
Revenues rocketed 35% in the six months to September end to £7.2bn, while operating profits were 45% stronger at £187m, driven primarily by a strong performance at emissions control division Clean Air, the company’s biggest unit.

The company, which traces its roots back to 1817, is undergoing a major overhaul, including selling its catalyst technologies business to Honeywell and the acquisition earlier this year of stationary emissions specialist Cormetech, which has a particular strong focus on data centres.

Liam Condon, chief executive, said the first half had been "an important first step forward" in the company’s transformation. "We have fundamentally reshaped our portfolio and made significant returns to shareholders," he said. "We have made an encouraging start in our integration of Cormetech…[and] our strong financial performance in the first half reflects positive business momentum and rigorous strategic execution."

Looking to the rest of the year, and Johnson Matthey now expects high single digit percentage growth in group underlying operating profit, up from previous guidance for low-to-mid single digit percentage growth. The forecast is based on constant precious metal prices and currencies, and strips out both catalyst technologies and Cormetech.

It also flagged a potential £35m benefit from platinum group metal prices, if they remain at their current levels for the remainder of the fiscal year.

As at 0915 GMT, the FTSE 250 stock had put on 3% at 2,390p.

Johnson Matthey also announced on Thursday that chief operating officer Richard Pike was stepping down from 31 December "to pursue the next chapter of his career". The current head of strategy and corporate development, Oliver Krotoszyner will succeed him.

data.title: Kuaishou Swings to Quarterly Loss as AI Spending Intensifies
data.description:
By Kimberley Kao

Chinese short-video company Kuaishou Technology warned of continued headwinds as it swung to a loss in the third quarter, dragged by increased spending on its artificial-intelligence business.

The Beijing-based company on Thursday reported a net loss of 959 million yuan, equivalent to $143.8 million, for the three months ended September.

That missed the 163.2 million yuan loss expected by analysts in a Visible Alpha poll. Adjusting for share-based compensation expenses, net fair-value changes on investments and finance costs on redemption financial liabilities, net profit fell 84%, Kuaishou said.

The business was affected by intense external competition and a changing consumer environment, it said.

Like its Chinese tech peers, Kuaishou, one of China's largest short-video platform, has been spending big on AI as industry competition heats up.

Revenue fell 11% from a year earlier to 31.59 billion yuan, slightly missing market expectations of 32.94 billion yuan.

Kuaishou's other services segment, which includes Kling AI, posted revenue growth of 1.5% for the third quarter, as higher revenue from games and Kling AI offset a decline in e-commerce revenue.

That compared with an 11% decline in revenue from online marketing services, and a 19% drop in revenue from its live-streaming business.

"The near-term operating environment remains challenging, with relatively conservative consumers' and marketers' spending sentiments and intense competition," the company said.

Kuaishou said it expects its Kling investments and broader AI strategy to weigh on profitability in the near term. Revenue and profits may remain under pressure in the fourth quarter, it said.

data.title: Spain's Far Right Poses Threat to Migration Boon — Market Talk
data.description: The biggest risk to Spain's economy from a potential right-wing government is disruption to migration and a resultant squeeze on the labor force, economists at JPMorgan write in a note to clients. The country is set to hold elections next week, with surveys pointing to a coalition between the center-right People's Party and far-right Vox. The latter would likely look to crack down on irregular migration and block pathways to regularization, posing an obstacle to the labor boom that has helped Spain's economy outperform in recent years, JPM says. Still, there are constraints on how much a right-wing administration could do to reduce migration, the bank says, noting potential EU legal issues as well as recognition on the part of party leaders that migrants are key to the workforce in an era of demographic challenge. (joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby)

data.title: Wall Street $500B financing pledge for Nvidia fails to materialize- report
data.description:
A pledge from firms to secure $500B in financing for Nvidia chips, secured by Jensen Huang earlier this year, has failed to materialize, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

Huang, who left the chipmaking giant after a slew of extramarital affairs, got pledges from Apollo Global Management , Blackstone , BlackRock , Brookfield Asset Management , Goldman Sachs and KKR in August.

The money would go to Nvidia customers, including OpenAI and Anthropic as well as smaller ones to buy the chips they needed.

However, no capital has been deployed, WSJ said, citing unnamed sources, and investor doubt is creeping in about whether the program will actually pan out, especially with Huang’s exit and the cautious approach of finance head and current interim CEO Colette Kress.

“We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” Kress said on Tuesday on Nvidia’s earnings call.

data.title: Treasury, Eurozone Bond Yields Edge Higher — Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields turned higher in European trade on Thursday as the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a faster pace.

Eurozone bond yields were slightly higher ahead of heavy bond supply from Spain and France. Spain will auction 4.5 billion euros to 5.5 billion euros ($4.94 billion to $6.04 billion) in three bonds, including a new seven-year one. France will offer a combined 11.25 billion euros to 13.75 billion euros in a total of eight nominal and inflation-linked bonds.

The 10-year Treasury yield last traded 1.9 basis points higher at 5.084%, while 10-year German Bund yield edged up 0.9 basis points to 3.380%, according to Tradeweb.

"Ten-year Bund yields remain within their recently established range just below 3.4%, but volatility is picking up amid hawkish central bank talk and shaky risk sentiment," said Hauke Siemssen, rates strategist at Commerzbank, in a note.

Minutes of the latest Fed rate-setting meeting, where the Fed left interest rates unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase of half a percentage point in December. The committee's discussion of inflation revealed increasing concern of broadening price pressure amid strong growth in economic activity, Stuart Paul, U.S. economist at UBS, said in a note.

The minutes increased market expectations of a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike at the December meeting. Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and an 8% likelihood of a 50-basis-point tightening, according to LSEG. A 50-basis-point hike was priced with a 2% probability on Wednesday.

"An unyielding Federal Reserve continues to govern fixed income and currency markets," Patrick Munnelly, market strategist at Tickmill Group, said in a note. "Wednesday's October [Federal Open Market Committee] minutes confirmed that nearly all officials anticipate further rate hikes to return inflation to target, with two participants even floating the risk of a 50bps move in December if price pressures persist," he said.

Crucially, policymakers took comfort from tighter market-implied rate paths doing the Fed's heavy lifting--meaning any sustained AI-driven easing in financial conditions risks provoking a sharper monetary pushback, Munnelly added.

The Treasury will conduct a $19 billion auction of 10-year Treasury inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, on Thursday.

Despite the backdrop of higher real yields, cheap valuations, and improving liquidity, J.P. Morgan analysts think the hawkish Fed backdrop and amount of supply in the 10-year sector means the auction "will need more of a concession to be digested smoothly."

Write to Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com
